chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a free man performing li'an with his female slave. He said, 'Yes, if her master is the one who married her to him.'
ai.seo_question: Who performs li'an when a free man marries a female slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisdictional nuance in *Li'an* (mutual cursing) involving a *Umm al-Walad* or slave woman, specifying that the master who contracted the marriage holds the authority to initiate the procedure. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the *Mawla* (master) retains specific marital rights over the slave, distinct from the slave's own agency, ensuring the legal validity of the divorce process. It highlights the interplay between ownership (*Milk*) and marital contract (*Nikah*) in classical fiqh.
